M8 (schema 0.8, integration/migrate_v07_to_v08.py): blood_pressure SBP/DBP drawn from NFHS-5 age-band×sex bivariate normals (means: PLOS ONE 2025 doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0332226; per-band SDs DERIVED from that paper's mean/95%-CI/n and cross-validated to within 0.8% against the independently published NFHS-5 male overall SDs, PMC11068163; SBP/DBP correlation r=0.7255 DERIVED from that paper's SD(SBP)/SD(DBP)/SD(pulse-pressure) triple, not assumed), restricted to the region the hypertension label's OWN published definition implies (SBP≥140 and/or DBP≥90 and/or on antihypertensive) -- so BP is CONDITIONAL on that already-primary label and is NEVER used to re-derive it, and a TREATED hypertensive's BP is left unconstrained rather than forced high; a pulse-pressure floor of 20 mmHg is an EXPLICIT ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION (it removes a 2% tail of clinically absurd narrow-PP records a Gaussian copula produces), no upper cap; ages above source coverage (men>54, women>49) hold the oldest band constant, flagged per record via blood_pressure.extrapolated_beyond_source_age_range; encounters contain ONE synthetic_baseline_assessment -- a structural container for this record's single measurement cross-section, NOT an observed healthcare contact (no visit/admission/appointment/follow-up is generated: no Indian utilization evidence exists); clinical_timeline gains reference_id and indexes that encounter, and still emits no diagnosis-onset, medication-start or follow-up event; height_cm/weight_kg STILL null after 6 failed research attempts for a national mean+SD of Indian adult height by sex (M4-0 ×3, M8 ×3), so BMI remains the evidence-primary anthropometric; family_history STILL null -- an open human scope decision, not an evidence gap; ECG unchanged and still metadata-only with signal_available=false (D003); echo unchanged.
